analysis.investment_thesis: A 2024-era SME jewellery IPO trading at 18x earnings on a 0.22% ROE is priced for a fantasy that the fundamentals do not support. The risk of permanent capital loss far outweighs the upside at INR 85.70.
key_strengths: Promoter skin in the game at 56.33% ownership
Asset-light jewellery manufacturing in a growing Indian consumption category
Small base (INR 52 Cr m-cap) leaves theoretical room to scale
key_risks: ROE of 0.22% indicates the business earns essentially nothing on equity — P/E of 18 is illusory
Recent SME IPO at cycle peak; jewellery working-capital cycles crush undercapitalized players in downturns
Negligible institutional ownership (FII 2%, DII 2.47%) = no price discovery, poor liquidity, manipulation risk
red_flags: 0.22% ROE is a statistical rounding error — either earnings are near-zero or equity was just inflated by IPO proceeds
Classic late-cycle SME IPO: small jewellery maker listing into euphoric retail demand
P/E of 18 on near-zero ROE implies a P/B that makes no economic sense
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Second-level thinking here is brutal: the market looks at "18x P/E, jewellery, India consumption story" and buys. But an 18x multiple on a 0.22% ROE means the business is destroying economic value — you are paying a growth multiple for a company that barely earns its cost of capital, let alone exceeds it. With INR 52 Cr market cap and ~INR 2.9 Cr implied net profit, this is a micro-cap whose reported earnings are immaterial and almost certainly volatile. Jewellery manufacturing is a brutally competitive, working-capital-heavy, margin-thin business dominated by Titan, Kalyan, Senco and thousands of unorganized players — a 2018-vintage entrant has no discernible moat.

Where are we in the cycle? SME IPOs in India are in full euphoric mode — exactly the regime where Marks would counsel maximum skepticism. The asymmetry is wrong: downside is 50-80% (typical SME IPO mean-reversion) while upside requires a heroic 10x+ improvement in ROE that has no evidence behind it. With only 4.47% institutional float, there is no sophisticated capital setting price — just retail sentiment. No margin of safety exists. Pass, and wait for the cycle to turn and the price to reflect reality.
